app.title: Hypnos — anesthetic PK/PD model divergence
app.summary: A person sets up a virtual patient and a dosing schedule in a sidebar: the drug, body size, organ function, bolus and infusion, the time horizon, and optionally seeded prediction bands and uncertainty in the weight value. The dashboard runs every published model for that drug on the same scenario. It overlays their plasma and effect-site curves, greys out models whose applicability range the patient falls outside, and reports how far apart the models are at the peak and which pair drives the gap. With bands on, it also shows whether the models can be told apart beyond their own stated variability, and how the uncertainty splits into structural, between-subject, residual and covariate shares. Further panels apply the same treatment to drug interactions, local anesthetics, inhaled agents, reversal agents, children and a declared genotype.

task.text: Measure how much published population models disagree when they predict the same scenario, and judge whether that disagreement goes beyond each model's own stated uncertainty.

data.text: A curated library of published parameter sets for population models, with citations, confidence tiers, applicability ranges and variability terms, simulated forward over time for a scenario the person sets
data.item: a published population model of one drug, simulated as a concentration or effect curve over time for the chosen patient and dose

stage.text: comparing published models against each other before choosing one for a study or simulation

mechanism.text: Sidebar inputs drive a single simulation of every eligible model. Its results feed overlaid line charts with optional percentile ribbons, a status list of models that were kept, greyed out or unavailable, and summary metrics for the divergence and the variance decomposition. Self-contained panels further down repeat the same simulate-and-overlay approach for other subsystems, each with its own column of controls.

field.text: population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model simulation and comparison in anesthesia pharmacology

workflow.name: run competing published models on one scenario and measure how much they disagree

steps.step: set up the scenario to test
steps.here: Sidebar: pick a drug, set age, weight, height and sex, add organ function (Child-Pugh, CrCl, albumin, ejection fraction), and enter bolus and infusion text from drug-appropriate defaults, plus a time horizon

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Models whose applicability range the patient violates are greyed out and tiered down to D, with reasons; models without a kernel are listed as unavailable
Effect-site and plasma concentration curves from every included model are overlaid on shared time axes, each labelled with its tier

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: A metric for peak divergence across models (absolute and relative spread), the driver pair furthest apart at the peak, each model's published MDAPE, and a table of time to peak effect with ke0

steps.step: add uncertainty and test whether the difference survives it
steps.here: Turning on seeded 5–95% bands (with a seed and Monte-Carlo sample count), or a weight SD, draws ribbons only for models that publish variability. The view then reports a separation index, a variance-share bar chart, the reducible vs irreducible split, and a PK variability band carried through into effect (BIS)

steps.step: repeat the comparison for special cases
steps.here: Separate panels for propofol–remifentanil synergy, local-anesthetic absorption by injection site against toxicity-threshold ranges, inhaled-agent MAC and wash-in/out, reversal agents, a child patient by post-menstrual age, and a declared genotype

distinctive: Each model has an applicability range, and a patient outside it greys the model out and forces its confidence tier down to D. The set of eligible models changes as the patient changes.
Prediction bands are drawn only for models that publish between-subject variability. The other models stay as dashed point lines and are named, never given a borrowed band.
Uncertainty is split into structural (which model), between-subject, residual and covariate shares, and also into reducible vs irreducible, at the moment of peak disagreement.
The interface only simulates forward from a dose the person enters. It never computes a dose, and it repeats this in its labels throughout.
Confidence tiers carry through composed simulations: a PK model, an effect link and an interaction surface together take the worst tier among their components.
